summary: Provides several certificate policy identifiers (object identifiers) that can be used to test software that processes certificates, so implementations can check how they handle certificate policies.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7229 provides eight certificate policy identifiers for testing software. They are not for public Internet certificates, and certificates that use them should not be trusted.

questions: object identifiers for testing certificate policies
what are the test certificate policy identifiers
subtitle: Eight certificate policy identifiers intended only for software testing.

tldr.problem: Software that handles certificates needs policy identifiers for testing. Using these identifiers in public Internet certificates is not intended.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7229 defines eight object identifiers under id-TEST, which is under id-pkix at arc 13. They can test processing of certificate policy extensions and related extensions.
tldr.outcome: The identifiers are for testing only. The RFC says no confidence should be placed in a certificate that uses them.

today: RFC 7229 is an Informational document that defines certificate policy identifiers for testing certificate-handling software. It does not define identifiers for production certificates.

sections.title: Why Test Identifiers Are Needed
sections.content: RFC 7229 supplies certificate policy identifiers for testing certificate-handling software. The identifiers follow the certificate profile in RFC 5280 and can be used to test processing of certificate policy, policy constraints, and policy mapping extensions. They are not intended for the public Internet.
sections.plainLanguage: Software needs example policy labels to test how it handles certificates. This document supplies labels for that testing, not for public use.

sections.title: The Eight Test Identifiers
sections.content: The document places the id-TEST node below id-pkix with the value 13. It defines eight child identifiers named id-TEST-certPolicyOne through id-TEST-certPolicyEight, with final values 1 through 8. They use the ASN.1 object identifier format.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC names eight test policy identifiers beneath id-TEST. Each has a different final number, from 1 through 8.

sections.title: Do Not Trust Test Certificates
sections.content: RFC 7229 does not identify certificate policies for production use in the Internet public key infrastructure. It says no confidence should be placed in any certificate that uses these identifiers because they are intended only for testing. The document requires no further IANA action.
sections.plainLanguage: These identifiers are for tests only. A certificate that uses one should not be trusted.
